plan_areas.community_vision: The community's vision for Anne Arundel County is to embrace its rich Chesapeake culture and heritage while leveraging emerging opportunities to become a place where all residents are proud to live, work, learn, and play. The plan aspires to create resilient and environmentally-sound communities, supported by new and improved infrastructure. It aims for strategic economic growth and redevelopment, focusing on innovation and technology while supporting traditional businesses such as agriculture and marine trades. A key aspect is protecting the unique character of communities and enhancing public access to natural resources, all while fostering an inclusive, equitable, and responsive government that ensures opportunity for all.

In the coming years, Annapolis will be a more equitable, healthy, and resilient city. It will be a more walkable and connected city where multiple safe and reliable transportation options reduce personal vehicle dependency. It will be a city which prioritizes public investments in its most socially vulnerable communities; a city which expands housing options accessible to residents of all income levels; and a city which grows a community of diverse local entrepreneurs aided by inclusive economic programs and opportunities. Annapolis will be a city which prioritizes the preservation, restoration, maintenance, and enhancement of its natural resources, particularly when planning for new development. It will be a city which ensures that all residents have access to high quality recreational amenities particularly public water access; and it will be a city which values its cultural life through support for arts initiatives, artists and arts organizations, and citywide historic preservation efforts. And Annapolis will be climate ready. Its infrastructure will be designed to withstand or adapt to the impacts from climate change. The city will protect its communities and institutions most at risk of climate impacts; and the city will reduce its carbon emissions through a variety of coordinated policies, programs, and investments.

In the coming years, Annapolis will be a more equitable, healthy, and resilient city. It will be a more walkable and connected city where multiple safe and reliable transportation options reduce personal vehicle dependency. It will be a city which prioritizes public investments in its most socially vulnerable communities; a city which expands housing options accessible to residents of all income levels; and a city which grows a community of diverse local entrepreneurs aided by inclusive economic programs and opportunities. Annapolis will be a city which prioritizes the preservation, restoration, maintenance, and enhancement of its natural resources, particularly when planning for new development. It will be a city which ensures that all residents have access to high quality recreational amenities particularly public water access; and it will be a city which values its cultural life through support for arts initiatives, artists and arts organizations, and citywide historic preservation efforts. plan_areas.community_vision: The community's vision for Anne Arundel County is to embrace its rich Chesapeake culture and heritage while leveraging emerging opportunities to become a place where all residents are proud to live, work, learn, and play. The plan aspires to create resilient and environmentally-sound communities, supported by new and improved infrastructure. It aims for strategic economic growth and redevelopment, focusing on innovation and technology while supporting traditional businesses such as agriculture and marine trades. A key aspect is protecting the unique character of communities and enhancing public access to natural resources, all while fostering an inclusive, equitable, and responsive government that ensures opportunity for all.

In the coming years, Annapolis will be a more equitable, healthy, and resilient city. It will be a more walkable and connected city where multiple safe and reliable transportation options reduce personal vehicle dependency. It will be a city which prioritizes public investments in its most socially vulnerable communities; a city which expands housing options accessible to residents of all income levels; and a city which grows a community of diverse local entrepreneurs aided by inclusive economic programs and opportunities. Annapolis will be a city which prioritizes the preservation, restoration, maintenance, and enhancement of its natural resources, particularly when planning for new development. It will be a city which ensures that all residents have access to high quality recreational amenities particularly public water access; and it will be a city which values its cultural life through support for arts initiatives, artists and arts organizations, and citywide historic preservation efforts. And Annapolis will be climate ready. Its infrastructure will be designed to withstand or adapt to the impacts from climate change. The city will protect its communities and institutions most at risk of climate impacts; and the city will reduce its carbon emissions through a variety of coordinated policies, programs, and investments.

plan_areas.community_vision: In 2035, Prince George’s County is the community of choice for families, businesses, and workers in the region. It is distinguished by strong, green, and healthy communities; a competitive, innovative, and adaptive economy; vibrant and walkable mixed-use centers; quality open space; restored ecosystems; and iconic destinations. It meets the diverse needs of all Prince Georgians and embraces and builds on the momentum generated by new residents, technology, and business opportunities.

The Suitland-Naylor Road Metro Station Area envisions a future as a vital and livable community, leveraging its strategic location as a gateway to Prince George's County from Washington D.C. The community aims to transform into a vibrant, mixed-use hub centered around its Metro stations, attracting new investment, residents, and businesses. Key priorities include increasing economic vitality through commercial revitalization and workforce development, enhancing livability by improving housing stock and public safety, and increasing prosperity for households by expanding access to fresh food, healthcare, and recreational opportunities. The plan serves as a multi-year investment strategy to create a more sustainable, connected, and thriving place for all residents.

Montgomery County aspires to accommodate future growth by becoming more urban, diverse, and interconnected. The vision is for a future with economically competitive and complete communities that foster a stronger sense of trust and inclusiveness among people from different backgrounds. The plan guides the county to leverage growth and redevelopment to create places that improve environmental quality, support active lifestyles, encourage interaction, and address historic inequities. It seeks to make difficult decisions and take bold steps to adapt to social, environmental, demographic, and economic shifts, ensuring the county continues to be a desirable place to live and work.

The community's vision is guided by the Thrive Montgomery 2050 plan, which aims to create a future where Montgomery County is equitable, environmentally resilient, and economically competitive. The plan emphasizes racial equity and social justice by creating integrated and just communities, fights climate change through compact, walkable development with enhanced transit, and strengthens economic competitiveness by creating desirable places to live and work, connecting a diverse population to economic opportunities.

In the coming years, Annapolis will be a more equitable, healthy, and resilient city. It will be a more walkable and connected city where multiple safe and reliable transportation options reduce personal vehicle dependency. It will be a city which prioritizes public investments in its most socially vulnerable communities; a city which expands housing options accessible to residents of all income levels; and a city which grows a community of diverse local entrepreneurs aided by inclusive economic programs and opportunities. Annapolis will be a city which prioritizes the preservation, restoration, maintenance, and enhancement of its natural resources, particularly when planning for new development. It will be a city which ensures that all residents have access to high quality recreational amenities particularly public water access; and it will be a city which values its cultural life through support for arts initiatives, artists and arts organizations, and citywide historic preservation efforts. And Annapolis will be climate ready. Its infrastructure will be designed to withstand or adapt to the impacts from climate change. plan_areas.community_vision: In 2040, Frederick County is a vibrant and unique community where people live, work, and thrive while enjoying a strong sense of place and belonging. The community ensures all people can be successful and enjoy a high quality of life, free from poverty. It provides interesting and fulfilling jobs, embraces businesses of all sizes for a strong economy, and values its traditional industries like agriculture while seizing future opportunities. A multi-modal transportation system moves people and goods efficiently, and the county is a safe place to live with excellent public education and lifelong learning opportunities. Planning enhances towns and neighborhoods while preserving farms, history, and the environment.

OVER 85,000 PEOPLE CALL THE CITY OF FREDERICK HOME. IT IS A PLACE WHERE PEOPLE HAVE CHOSEN TO WORK, LEARN, INNOVATE, AND RELAX. FREDERICK IS NATIONALLY RECOGNIZED FOR THOUGHTFUL MANAGED SUSTAINABLE URBAN DEVELOPMENT. PROSPERITY IS BALANCED WITH HOUSING, EMPLOYMENT, AND CULTURAL OPPORTUNITIES FOR EVERYONE. OUR VIBRANT DOWNTOWN AND LIVABLE NEIGHBORHOODS WELCOME NEW RESIDENTS AND CREATIVE ENTREPRENEURS. EMPLOYERS LARGE AND SMALL PROVIDE COMPETITIVE EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITIES FOR THE CITY OF FREDERICK’S WORKFORCE. WELL-COORDINATED TRANSPORTATION CHOICES ALLOW MOVEMENT AROUND, WITHIN, AND BEYOND FREDERICK TO NEARBY METROPOLITAN AREAS. FREDERICK IS RICH IN THE DIVERSITY OF TALENTS, CULTURES, AND LIFE STORIES THAT CONNECT US WITH EACH OTHER. ALL VOICES ARE ENCOURAGED AND RESPECTED, FOSTERING ONE OF THE MOST CIVICALLY ENGAGED CITIES IN AMERICA. STEEPED IN HISTORY, FREDERICK IS A PROGRESSIVE, WELCOMING, AND AUTHENTICALLY CHARMING CITY.

The City of Frederick is committed to improving the quality of life by strengthening its neighborhoods. The City will maintain a predictable development pattern where each part of the community has a distinct character. Growth will be planned to enhance the quality of life for new and existing residents while strengthening the economic health of the City, guided by its 'CommUNITY 2030' strategic plan.

plan_areas.community_vision: In 2035, Prince George’s County is the community of choice for families, businesses, and workers in the region. It meets the diverse needs of all Prince Georgians and embraces and builds on the momentum generated by new residents, technology, and business opportunities.

Montgomery County aspires to accommodate future growth by becoming more urban, diverse, and interconnected. The vision is for a future with economically competitive and complete communities that foster a stronger sense of trust and inclusiveness among people from different backgrounds. The plan guides the county to leverage growth and redevelopment to create places that improve environmental quality, support active lifestyles, encourage interaction, and address historic inequities. It seeks to make difficult decisions and take bold steps to adapt to social, environmental, demographic, and economic shifts, ensuring the county continues to be a desirable place to live and work.

The community's vision is guided by the Thrive Montgomery 2050 plan, which aims to create a future where Montgomery County is equitable, environmentally resilient, and economically competitive. plan_areas.community_vision: The community's vision for Anne Arundel County is to embrace its rich Chesapeake culture and heritage while leveraging emerging opportunities to become a place where all residents are proud to live, work, learn, and play. The plan aspires to create resilient and environmentally-sound communities, supported by new and improved infrastructure. It aims for strategic economic growth and redevelopment, focusing on innovation and technology while supporting traditional businesses such as agriculture and marine trades. A key aspect is protecting the unique character of communities and enhancing public access to natural resources, all while fostering an inclusive, equitable, and responsive government that ensures opportunity for all.

Howard County is envisioned as a welcoming and inclusive community offering a high quality of life with a top-tier school system, thriving neighborhoods, abundant open space, innovative businesses, and diverse recreational, cultural, and housing opportunities. The community values its eclectic mix of environments, from rural farms to an urban downtown, and strives to accommodate future growth while retaining its unique character. The vision emphasizes sustainable development, environmental stewardship, and well-maintained infrastructure, ensuring policies and investments respect the natural environment, historic resources, and diverse populations in an equitable, predictable, sustainable, and achievable manner.

The vision for North Laurel-Savage focuses on transforming the Route 1 corridor into a vibrant, mixed-use area with enhanced economic opportunities, while preserving and promoting the historic character of Savage. The community aims to improve connectivity and safety for pedestrians, cyclists, and transit users, connecting neighborhoods to amenities like the MARC stations and local parks. Key priorities include increasing the supply of affordable and accessible housing, enhancing quality of life through new community facilities like a public pool, and protecting environmental assets through restoration and green infrastructure projects. The overarching goal is to create a well-defined sense of place with a strong brand identity, improved public services, and greater civic engagement.

Central to this vision is creating a sustainable economic future that does not rely on becoming a bedroom community, but rather on fostering local job creation and bolstering the county's fiscal health to support necessary infrastructure and services.

Harford County's vision is to accommodate and focus growth in a manner that maintains rural areas, strengthens communities with an emphasis on sustainable development, and enhances the quality of life. The plan serves as a policy guide for implementing innovative ideas that will help build strong communities, grow a competitive economic base, and preserve the county's rich heritage for generations to come.

The overall vision for the Comprehensive Plan is to maintain the historical character while embracing growth that is occurring in and around the Town’s municipal boundary. By utilizing land use and growth management practices based on shared principles agreed upon by residents and Town Officials, Leonardtown can achieve a balanced development. These principles include protecting and perpetuating the town’s small-town charm while ensuring it remains the hub for St. Mary’s County’s government, education, health services, and judicial systems. Key elements of this vision include a vital and thriving downtown, a sustained appreciation and commitment to the protection of the town’s historic resources, broader public access to waterfront resources, provision of a wide range of services and events, and management of anticipated growth to protect and preserve the “small town” character.

plan_areas.community_vision: In 2035, Prince George’s County is the community of choice for families, businesses, and workers in the region. It is distinguished by strong, green, and healthy communities; a competitive, innovative, and adaptive economy; vibrant and walkable mixed-use centers; quality open space; restored ecosystems; and iconic destinations. It meets the diverse needs of all Prince Georgians and embraces and builds on the momentum generated by new residents, technology, and business opportunities.

Montgomery County aspires to accommodate future growth by becoming more urban, diverse, and interconnected. The vision is for a future with economically competitive and complete communities that foster a stronger sense of trust and inclusiveness among people from different backgrounds. The plan guides the county to leverage growth and redevelopment to create places that improve environmental quality, support active lifestyles, encourage interaction, and address historic inequities. It seeks to make difficult decisions and take bold steps to adapt to social, environmental, demographic, and economic shifts, ensuring the county continues to be a desirable place to live and work.

The community's vision is guided by the Thrive Montgomery 2050 plan, which aims to create a future where Montgomery County is equitable, environmentally resilient, and economically competitive. The plan emphasizes racial equity and social justice by creating integrated and just communities, fights climate change through compact, walkable development with enhanced transit, and strengthens economic competitiveness by creating desirable places to live and work, connecting a diverse population to economic opportunities.

plan_areas.community_vision: Montgomery County aspires to accommodate future growth by becoming more urban, diverse, and interconnected. The vision is for a future with economically competitive and complete communities that foster a stronger sense of trust and inclusiveness among people from different backgrounds. The plan guides the county to leverage growth and redevelopment to create places that improve environmental quality, support active lifestyles, encourage interaction, and address historic inequities. It seeks to make difficult decisions and take bold steps to adapt to social, environmental, demographic, and economic shifts, ensuring the county continues to be a desirable place to live and work.

The community's vision is guided by the Thrive Montgomery 2050 plan, which aims to create a future where Montgomery County is equitable, environmentally resilient, and economically competitive. The plan emphasizes racial equity and social justice by creating integrated and just communities, fights climate change through compact, walkable development with enhanced transit, and strengthens economic competitiveness by creating desirable places to live and work, connecting a diverse population to economic opportunities.

The Long Reach community envisions a vibrant, revitalized Village Center serving as a hub for arts, culture, education, and economic empowerment. The community's goal is to become a stronger, more connected place through beautification, placemaking, and attracting new businesses. A key part of this vision is enhancing multi-modal transportation with a focus on complete streets to improve safety and accessibility for pedestrians, cyclists, and transit users, thereby connecting neighborhoods to the Village Center and other key community destinations.

The vision for North Laurel-Savage focuses on transforming the Route 1 corridor into a vibrant, mixed-use area with enhanced economic opportunities, while preserving and promoting the historic character of Savage. The community aims to improve connectivity and safety for pedestrians, cyclists, and transit users, connecting neighborhoods to amenities like the MARC stations and local parks. Key priorities include increasing the supply of affordable and accessible housing, enhancing quality of life through new community facilities like a public pool, and protecting environmental assets through restoration and green infrastructure projects. The overarching goal is to create a well-defined sense of place with a strong brand identity, improved public services, and greater civic engagement.

plan_areas.community_vision: In 2035, Prince George’s County is the community of choice for families, businesses, and workers in the region. It is distinguished by strong, green, and healthy communities; a competitive, innovative, and adaptive economy; vibrant and walkable mixed-use centers; quality open space; restored ecosystems; and iconic destinations. It meets the diverse needs of all Prince Georgians and embraces and builds on the momentum generated by new residents, technology, and business opportunities.

The City of Glenarden's Sustainable Community Action Plan is a multi-year investment strategy developed through community visioning sessions. The plan outlines a strategic set of revitalization initiatives and projects that local partners believe will increase the economic vitality and livability of their community, increase prosperity for local households, and improve the health of the surrounding environment. The city is seeking assistance to make revitalization improvements across six key areas: Environment, Local Economy, Housing, Quality of Life, Transportation, and Land Use/Local Planning.

plan_areas.community_vision: The community's vision for Anne Arundel County is to embrace its rich Chesapeake culture and heritage while leveraging emerging opportunities to become a place where all residents are proud to live, work, learn, and play. The plan aspires to create resilient and environmentally-sound communities, supported by new and improved infrastructure. It aims for strategic economic growth and redevelopment, focusing on innovation and technology while supporting traditional businesses such as agriculture and marine trades. A key aspect is protecting the unique character of communities and enhancing public access to natural resources, all while fostering an inclusive, equitable, and responsive government that ensures opportunity for all.

In the coming years, Annapolis will be a more equitable, healthy, and resilient city. It will be a more walkable and connected city where multiple safe and reliable transportation options reduce personal vehicle dependency. It will be a city which prioritizes public investments in its most socially vulnerable communities; a city which expands housing options accessible to residents of all income levels; and a city which grows a community of diverse local entrepreneurs aided by inclusive economic programs and opportunities. Annapolis will be a city which prioritizes the preservation, restoration, maintenance, and enhancement of its natural resources, particularly when planning for new development. It will be a city which ensures that all residents have access to high quality recreational amenities particularly public water access; and it will be a city which values its cultural life through support for arts initiatives, artists and arts organizations, and citywide historic preservation efforts. And Annapolis will be climate ready. Its infrastructure will be designed to withstand or adapt to the impacts from climate change. The city will protect its communities and institutions most at risk of climate impacts; and the city will reduce its carbon emissions through a variety of coordinated policies, programs, and investments.

The North Brentwood community envisions a future that honors its unique history as the first incorporated African American town in Prince George's County while fostering economic growth and environmental resilience. The plan aims to transform the area into a historic tourist attraction, centered around revitalized assets like Sis's Tavern. Key goals include redeveloping the Route 1 commercial corridor to attract new businesses, improving housing conditions and creating options for seniors to age in place, and implementing comprehensive strategies to mitigate chronic flooding. The community strives to maintain its small-town, walkable atmosphere while empowering residents and creating a more vibrant and sustainable place to live.

The Port Towns, comprised of Bladensburg, Colmar Manor, Cottage City, and Edmonston, envision a future as an environmentally friendly and economically vibrant area. The community aims to strengthen its small business and industrial sectors, capitalize on its rich history and natural assets like the Anacostia River to attract residents and visitors, and improve housing conditions and quality of life for its diverse population. Key goals include fostering a strong local economy by supporting existing industries, developing a skilled workforce through a new trade school, and enhancing their identity as a desirable place to live, work, and visit.

plan_areas.community_vision: In 2035, Prince George’s County is the community of choice for families, businesses, and workers in the region. It is distinguished by strong, green, and healthy communities; a competitive, innovative, and adaptive economy; vibrant and walkable mixed-use centers; quality open space; restored ecosystems; and iconic destinations. The Greater Camp Springs-Town of Morningside community envisions a future centered on revitalized, mixed-use, and walkable development, particularly around the Branch Avenue Metro Station. The plan aims to enhance economic competitiveness by attracting new businesses and services, while diversifying housing options with a focus on high-density transit-oriented projects. Key goals include improving environmental sustainability through enhanced stormwater management and an increased tree canopy, making transportation safer and more accessible for pedestrians and cyclists, and fostering a unique sense of place with improved parks, cultural programming, and healthier food options. The community seeks to become a more livable, prosperous, and sustainable area by addressing challenges like commercial vacancies, foreclosures, and the lack of grocery stores.

Key priorities include increasing economic vitality through commercial revitalization and workforce development, enhancing livability by improving housing stock and public safety, and increasing prosperity for households by expanding access to fresh food, healthcare, and recreational opportunities. The plan serves as a multi-year investment strategy to create a more sustainable, connected, and thriving place for all residents.

The overarching goal is to create a well-defined sense of place with a strong brand identity, improved public services, and greater civic engagement.

plan_areas.community_vision: Montgomery County aspires to accommodate future growth by becoming more urban, diverse, and interconnected. The vision is for a future with economically competitive and complete communities that foster a stronger sense of trust and inclusiveness among people from different backgrounds. The plan guides the county to leverage growth and redevelopment to create places that improve environmental quality, support active lifestyles, encourage interaction, and address historic inequities. It seeks to make difficult decisions and take bold steps to adapt to social, environmental, demographic, and economic shifts, ensuring the county continues to be a desirable place to live and work.

The community's vision is guided by the Thrive Montgomery 2050 plan, which aims to create a future where Montgomery County is equitable, environmentally resilient, and economically competitive. The plan emphasizes racial equity and social justice by creating integrated and just communities, fights climate change through compact, walkable development with enhanced transit, and strengthens economic competitiveness by creating desirable places to live and work, connecting a diverse population to economic opportunities.

The plan emphasizes economic growth by improving commercial corridors and leveraging its Arts District designation. It also prioritizes community well-being by improving housing quality, increasing mobility for pedestrians and cyclists, supporting seniors to age in place, and fostering an inclusive community through dedicated programs and a future community center.

The City of Hyattsville envisions a future as a racially and socioeconomically diverse community, experiencing significant residential and mixed-use growth in its commercial and transit-oriented corridors. The vision prioritizes a resilient local economy, a multi-modal transportation system with an emphasis on bicycle and pedestrian infrastructure, and the preservation and creation of affordable housing to ensure residents can stay in the city at all stages of life. This growth is guided by a commitment to sustainability and a planning process that reflects the community's evolving values.

The North Brentwood community envisions a future that honors its unique history as the first incorporated African American town in Prince George's County while fostering economic growth and environmental resilience. The plan aims to transform the area into a historic tourist attraction, centered around revitalized assets like Sis's Tavern. Key goals include redeveloping the Route 1 commercial corridor to attract new businesses, improving housing conditions and creating options for seniors to age in place, and implementing comprehensive strategies to mitigate chronic flooding. The community strives to maintain its small-town, walkable atmosphere while empowering residents and creating a more vibrant and sustainable place to live.

The Port Towns, comprised of Bladensburg, Colmar Manor, Cottage City, and Edmonston, envision a future as an environmentally friendly and economically vibrant area. The community aims to strengthen its small business and industrial sectors, capitalize on its rich history and natural assets like the Anacostia River to attract residents and visitors, and improve housing conditions and quality of life for its diverse population. Key goals include fostering a strong local economy by supporting existing industries, developing a skilled workforce through a new trade school, and enhancing their identity as a desirable place to live, work, and visit.

Greater Riverdale aspires to evolve into a well-connected, environmentally sustainable, and economically vibrant community. plan_areas.community_vision: Baltimore envisions a future of harmony, inclusivity, and prosperity, where every child can thrive regardless of their zip code and residents are empowered to shape the city's growth. The community aspires to heal historical divides, championing vibrant, safe neighborhoods for all ages. This vision includes transformational growth that respects cultural heritage, efficient and transparent governance, and a commitment to environmental stewardship and carbon neutrality. The city aims to nurture an economy where small businesses flourish, ensure community safety through collective action, and promote holistic well-being by acknowledging and rectifying past injustices.

Baltimore's vision is to foster inclusive economic growth and enhance its competitiveness by supporting its diverse neighborhoods, commercial corridors, and small businesses, particularly those owned by minorities and women. The city aims to create a more equitable, resilient, and sustainable community by building on existing assets, improving transportation efficiency, promoting diverse and affordable housing, and addressing historical disinvestment. The overarching goal is to create a Standard of Care that ensures the physical, social, emotional, and economic well-being for all residents, businesses, and stakeholders, guided by an equity lens in all planning and investment decisions.

The Cherry Hill Transformation Plan documents the community's vision to direct its own future change, building upon its rich history as a planned African-American suburb. The community aspires to become a place where residents can thrive without displacement, creating pathways out of poverty and building a strong, diverse community. Key elements of this vision include improving quality of life, increasing housing options, supporting Black-owned businesses, and implementing holistic transformation through public-private partnerships, potentially guided by the Purpose Built Communities model.

Reimagine Middle Branch is a community-driven initiative to reconnect South Baltimore with a system of world-class parks, trails, programs, and economic development plans along the 11-mile shoreline of the Middle Branch of the Patapsco River. By holistically addressing issues of environment, health, and equity, Reimagine Middle Branch strives to realize more than Baltimore’s next great waterfront. This initiative is fundamentally about equity and justice, resilience, and health—a transformation of place supported by new connections, jobs, wealth-generation, and quality of life amenities that extend beyond the built environment.

plan_areas.community_vision: Cecil County is on the cusp of significant change, with projections of rapid population and household growth by 2030. The community's vision is to manage this growth by incentivizing development within designated Growth Areas while discouraging it in rural areas to maintain the county's rural character and the viability of its agricultural industry. The plan aims to achieve a balance of residential development and employment opportunities, concentrating high-density, mixed-use development in areas with adequate public facilities. Central to this vision is creating a sustainable economic future that does not rely on becoming a bedroom community, but rather on fostering local job creation and bolstering the county's fiscal health to support necessary infrastructure and services.

Charlestown aims to revitalize its community by leveraging its rich colonial history and waterfront location. The vision includes developing parks and open spaces for recreation and environmental protection, attracting small businesses that complement its historic character, and enhancing tourism. Key goals involve improving infrastructure like stormwater management and pedestrian/bicycle connectivity, upgrading the housing stock with a focus on creating options for an aging population, and fostering a stronger sense of community by engaging all residents through diverse events and improved amenities. The town seeks to balance growth with preservation, channeling development appropriately while protecting its natural and historic resources.

properties.plan_areas: [{'area_name': 'Baltimore County', 'plan_year': '2030', 'community_vision': 'Baltimore County\'s Master Plan 2030 charts an aspirational course for the next decade, aiming to create livable, healthy communities in harmony with nature, with resilient economies, social equity, and strong regional ties. The plan shifts focus from traditional suburban development to a strategy of "retrofitting" underutilized commercial corridors and aging infrastructure. This involves creating walkable, mixed-use community centers, or "Nodes," to serve as the primary focus for redevelopment and investment. The vision is guided by six principles: a Livable Built Environment, Harmony with Nature, a Resilient Economy, Responsible Regionalism, Inclusive Planning, and a Healthy Community, all intended to ensure Baltimore County remains a safe, healthy, and prosperous place for all residents.'}]

childcare_need_quotes: In Frederick County, 34,688 households, 39 percent, could not afford basic needs such as housing, child care, food, transportation, health care and technology in 2016.
Support efforts to make high quality child care geographically and financially available to all children in the county.

An important outcome of this study is the Household Survival Budget that reflects the bare minimum cost to live and work in the modern economy and includes housing, child care, food, transportation, health care, technology, and taxes.

childcare_planning_quotes: The region continues to witness residential growth, evidenced by the increasing number of households. Currently, many new residential projects... are underway, contributing to a diverse range of housing options. Collectively, these projects will introduce around 2,000 new units to the corridor.

Continuing on an upward trend of growth, the Metropolitan Washington Council of Governments (MWCOG) estimates that Frederick’s population will grow by 1.8% per year until 2030, bringing the total to 89,600 (in 35,200 households)...
The City of Frederick has been building on average 680 units over the last ten years. This rate is an average increase over the previous ten-year period of 250 units annually, or 589.
One of the concerns consistently stressed by residents is the segregation of land uses and the lack of nearby supporting retail and service uses.
Notably, the region boasts the highest person per household ratio: 3.4 Average Household Size.

In the past 20 years, much of the growth in this area of the City [Northwest Area] has been suburban single-family, including Willow Brook, Tuscarora Creek, North Crossing, Clover Ridge, Cannon Bluff, Homewood, and Crum Farm and commercial corridors to serve the new neighborhoods.
Support efforts to make high quality child care geographically and financially available to all children in the county.
Examine regulations to ensure that the process to approve private school or business-located early childhood educational facilities is streamlined and meets all mandated educational standards.

Expand opportunities for early childhood education programs and services in the county to ensure that all children have access to high quality early educational programs, which are predictors to success later in life.

plan_areas.community_vision: In 2040, Frederick County is a vibrant and unique community where people live, work, and thrive while enjoying a strong sense of place and belonging. The community ensures all people can be successful and enjoy a high quality of life, free from poverty. It provides interesting and fulfilling jobs, embraces businesses of all sizes for a strong economy, and values its traditional industries like agriculture while seizing future opportunities. A multi-modal transportation system moves people and goods efficiently, and the county is a safe place to live with excellent public education and lifelong learning opportunities. Planning enhances towns and neighborhoods while preserving farms, history, and the environment.

OVER 85,000 PEOPLE CALL THE CITY OF FREDERICK HOME. IT IS A PLACE WHERE PEOPLE HAVE CHOSEN TO WORK, LEARN, INNOVATE, AND RELAX. FREDERICK IS NATIONALLY RECOGNIZED FOR THOUGHTFUL MANAGED SUSTAINABLE URBAN DEVELOPMENT. PROSPERITY IS BALANCED WITH HOUSING, EMPLOYMENT, AND CULTURAL OPPORTUNITIES FOR EVERYONE. OUR VIBRANT DOWNTOWN AND LIVABLE NEIGHBORHOODS WELCOME NEW RESIDENTS AND CREATIVE ENTREPRENEURS. EMPLOYERS LARGE AND SMALL PROVIDE COMPETITIVE EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITIES FOR THE CITY OF FREDERICK’S WORKFORCE. WELL-COORDINATED TRANSPORTATION CHOICES ALLOW MOVEMENT AROUND, WITHIN, AND BEYOND FREDERICK TO NEARBY METROPOLITAN AREAS. FREDERICK IS RICH IN THE DIVERSITY OF TALENTS, CULTURES, AND LIFE STORIES THAT CONNECT US WITH EACH OTHER. ALL VOICES ARE ENCOURAGED AND RESPECTED, FOSTERING ONE OF THE MOST CIVICALLY ENGAGED CITIES IN AMERICA. STEEPED IN HISTORY, FREDERICK IS A PROGRESSIVE, WELCOMING, AND AUTHENTICALLY CHARMING CITY.

The City of Frederick is committed to improving the quality of life by strengthening its neighborhoods. The City will maintain a predictable development pattern where each part of the community has a distinct character. Growth will be planned to enhance the quality of life for new and existing residents while strengthening the economic health of the City, guided by its 'CommUNITY 2030' strategic plan.

plan_areas.community_vision: In 2035, Prince George’s County is the community of choice for families, businesses, and workers in the region. It is distinguished by strong, green, and healthy communities; a competitive, innovative, and adaptive economy; vibrant and walkable mixed-use centers; quality open space; restored ecosystems; and iconic destinations. It meets the diverse needs of all Prince Georgians and embraces and builds on the momentum generated by new residents, technology, and business opportunities.

The Town of Berwyn Heights envisions a future as a vibrant, safe, and environmentally conscious community. The vision prioritizes enhancing the quality of life for all residents by preserving and expanding its urban tree canopy, improving stormwater management, and increasing transportation safety for pedestrians and cyclists. Economically, the town aims to revitalize its commercial corridor along Greenbelt Road, fostering a thriving business environment and exploring mixed-use redevelopment. Key goals include ensuring seniors can age in place through home repair assistance, improving housing affordability, and strengthening community engagement and participation across its diverse population.

The City of College Park's vision, guided by its 2021-2025 Strategic Plan and the University Community Vision 2030, is to become a top-tier university community. The city aims to be a diverse, vibrant, connected, and economically successful place that attracts and retains families, graduates, and a variety of businesses. Key goals include enhancing city services, celebrating diversity, preserving the environment, improving public safety, facilitating smart economic growth, fostering an inclusive and engaged community, expanding transportation options, and ensuring affordability for residents to live, work, and retire.

The City of Greenbelt aims to be a multi-year investment strategy and a strategic set of revitalization initiatives and projects that local partners believe will increase the economic vitality and livability of their community, increase prosperity for local households and improve the health of the surrounding environment. The plan focuses on environmental sustainability, economic development, multi-modal transportation, diverse housing options, and enhancing community health and quality of life. Key priorities include protecting the city's natural resources and historic character, supporting business growth, promoting affordable housing, ensuring safe transportation networks, and fostering an inclusive community through equitable planning.

plan_areas.community_vision: In 2035, Prince George’s County is the community of choice for families, businesses, and workers in the region. It is distinguished by strong, green, and healthy communities; a competitive, innovative, and adaptive economy; vibrant and walkable mixed-use centers; quality open space; restored ecosystems; and iconic destinations. It meets the diverse needs of all Prince Georgians and embraces and builds on the momentum generated by new residents, technology, and business opportunities.

The Town of Berwyn Heights envisions a future as a vibrant, safe, and environmentally conscious community. The vision prioritizes enhancing the quality of life for all residents by preserving and expanding its urban tree canopy, improving stormwater management, and increasing transportation safety for pedestrians and cyclists. Economically, the town aims to revitalize its commercial corridor along Greenbelt Road, fostering a thriving business environment and exploring mixed-use redevelopment. Key goals include ensuring seniors can age in place through home repair assistance, improving housing affordability, and strengthening community engagement and participation across its diverse population.

The City of College Park's vision, guided by its 2021-2025 Strategic Plan and the University Community Vision 2030, is to become a top-tier university community. The city aims to be a diverse, vibrant, connected, and economically successful place that attracts and retains families, graduates, and a variety of businesses. Key goals include enhancing city services, celebrating diversity, preserving the environment, improving public safety, facilitating smart economic growth, fostering an inclusive and engaged community, expanding transportation options, and ensuring affordability for residents to live, work, and retire.

The City of Greenbelt aims to be a multi-year investment strategy and a strategic set of revitalization initiatives and projects that local partners believe will increase the economic vitality and livability of their community, increase prosperity for local households and improve the health of the surrounding environment. The plan focuses on environmental sustainability, economic development, multi-modal transportation, diverse housing options, and enhancing community health and quality of life. Key priorities include protecting the city's natural resources and historic character, supporting business growth, promoting affordable housing, ensuring safe transportation networks, and fostering an inclusive community through equitable planning.

Chesapeake City has a distinguishing “sense of place” in terms of our heritage, layout, architecture, and picturesque setting. We are literally a bridge from Maryland’s western shore to eastern shore, separated by the Chesapeake & Delaware Canal and surrounded by farmland. The C&D is one of busiest canals in the United States, but our community does not rely on commercial shipping, ﬁsheries or manufacturing. Instead, our community is built on being the “Jewel of the Upper Shore” and the unique characteristics that draw people to live and visit Chesapeake City. We strive for a well-maintained community that provides quality services to our residents and visitors and to promote the heritage and natural resources of our community.

The community of Chesapeake City aims to move forward with smart growth while maintaining its historic character, charm, and rural atmosphere. The vision, guided by the Comprehensive Plan, encourages development that matches the character of the town, such as through its Traditional Neighborhood Development (TND) zoning. This includes planning for denser, more affordable multifamily homes closer to the existing older communities and less dense housing further from the town center, all while accommodating moderate growth enabled by new wastewater infrastructure.

plan_areas.community_vision: Carroll County is a great place to live, work, and play. The County conserves and promotes its unique rural agricultural heritage, protects its environmental resources, and promotes a balanced approach to new development and economic opportunities consistent with the fabric of its communities. Carroll County values, and citizens’ unalienable rights of life, liberty, and property, are respected, protected, and sustained.

Hampstead is the quintessential American small town. The community is clean, safe and attractive. The residential neighborhoods are quiet and well maintained. While many residents work outside the community, this is “home.” Hampstead is a great place for families. The public schools are excellent and the neighborhoods have very little crime. There are outstanding youth sports programs and a wide range of parks, playgrounds and recreational facilities. Hampstead is an active community. Residents walk, particularly around neighborhoods and on Main Street. While primarily a residential community, Hampstead has a thriving business district. The historic downtown is constantly improving. With many commuters using the Hampstead Bypass, the congestion on Main Street is much reduced. Heavier commercial uses are clustered at the north and south ends of Towns, preserving Hampstead’s “small town” feel. Industrial development is concentrated in and around existing industrial sites. These sites are buffered from the rest of the community. All new construction is held to high standards for design. While large enough to qualify as a “city,” Hampstead is committed to remaining a “town”-- in name and character. It is a community people are proud to call home.

The community's vision is to create a prosperous, vibrant community identity that provides a sense of place and achieves balanced growth, all while protecting its unique heritage. The citizens of Hampstead maintain a sense of pride in being a friendly, family-oriented, safe community with distinctive small-town charm, and seek to build on this foundation by attracting new businesses and residents.

plan_areas.community_vision: Baltimore envisions a future of harmony, inclusivity, and prosperity, where every child can thrive regardless of their zip code and residents are empowered to shape the city's growth. The community aspires to heal historical divides, championing vibrant, safe neighborhoods for all ages. This vision includes transformational growth that respects cultural heritage, efficient and transparent governance, and a commitment to environmental stewardship and carbon neutrality. The city aims to nurture an economy where small businesses flourish, ensure community safety through collective action, and promote holistic well-being by acknowledging and rectifying past injustices.

Baltimore's vision is to foster inclusive economic growth and enhance its competitiveness by supporting its diverse neighborhoods, commercial corridors, and small businesses, particularly those owned by minorities and women. The city aims to create a more equitable, resilient, and sustainable community by building on existing assets, improving transportation efficiency, promoting diverse and affordable housing, and addressing historical disinvestment. The overarching goal is to create a Standard of Care that ensures the physical, social, emotional, and economic well-being for all residents, businesses, and stakeholders, guided by an equity lens in all planning and investment decisions.

fresh_food_need_quotes: One of the most prominent is food insecurity or lack of access to healthy food. According to Feeding America, as of 2020, approximately 15.5 percent of the City’s residents are considered to suffer from food insecurity and subsequent effects.

Revitalization Goals: Use food as a catalyst to address health, economic, and environmental disparities in Healthy Food Priority Areas, areas where residents face compounded challenges in accessing healthy foods.

plan_areas.community_vision: In 2040, Frederick County is a vibrant and unique community where people live, work, and thrive while enjoying a strong sense of place and belonging. The community ensures all people can be successful and enjoy a high quality of life, free from poverty. It provides interesting and fulfilling jobs, embraces businesses of all sizes for a strong economy, and values its traditional industries like agriculture while seizing future opportunities. Planning enhances towns and neighborhoods while preserving farms, history, and the environment.

OVER 85,000 PEOPLE CALL THE CITY OF FREDERICK HOME. IT IS A PLACE WHERE PEOPLE HAVE CHOSEN TO WORK, LEARN, INNOVATE, AND RELAX. FREDERICK IS NATIONALLY RECOGNIZED FOR THOUGHTFUL MANAGED SUSTAINABLE URBAN DEVELOPMENT. PROSPERITY IS BALANCED WITH HOUSING, EMPLOYMENT, AND CULTURAL OPPORTUNITIES FOR EVERYONE. OUR VIBRANT DOWNTOWN AND LIVABLE NEIGHBORHOODS WELCOME NEW RESIDENTS AND CREATIVE ENTREPRENEURS. EMPLOYERS LARGE AND SMALL PROVIDE COMPETITIVE EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITIES FOR THE CITY OF FREDERICK’S WORKFORCE. WELL-COORDINATED TRANSPORTATION CHOICES ALLOW MOVEMENT AROUND, WITHIN, AND BEYOND FREDERICK TO NEARBY METROPOLITAN AREAS. FREDERICK IS RICH IN THE DIVERSITY OF TALENTS, CULTURES, AND LIFE STORIES THAT CONNECT US WITH EACH OTHER. ALL VOICES ARE ENCOURAGED AND RESPECTED, FOSTERING ONE OF THE MOST CIVICALLY ENGAGED CITIES IN AMERICA. STEEPED IN HISTORY, FREDERICK IS A PROGRESSIVE, WELCOMING, AND AUTHENTICALLY CHARMING CITY.

plan_areas.community_vision: The vision for Caroline County is to preserve its agricultural lands and rural character by directing future growth to its ten incorporated municipalities and existing population centers. This strategy aims to protect the county's natural resources, heritage, and water supply, while maintaining an agricultural land base that supports the local economy. By concentrating development, the county hopes to provide adequate community facilities and infrastructure efficiently, support its changing population, and encourage the redevelopment of existing housing.

It is Kent County’s vision to preserve its historic and cultural traditions, along with its high quality of life, while embracing sufficient economic opportunities to provide for the economic well-being of our citizens. This Plan recognizes that agriculture is the keystone to Kent County’s heritage and its future. Agriculture is the linchpin that buttresses the County’s economy, culture, history, and everyday experiences. Kent County cannot afford to have this key element damaged or displaced. This recognition of agriculture’s status as the highest and best use for much of the County is an essential tenet of this Plan.

PlanQAC’s vision is to preserve Queen Anne's County as a quintessential rural community that is a great place to live, a good place to work, a good neighbor and steward of its natural and cultural heritage, a protective community where development does not impair the quality of life, and a supportive county that provides the highest quality of education. During this planning cycle, the community finds itself nearing the limits of adequate public facilities including, transportation infrastructure on its state and local roads, the Chesapeake Bay Bridge, local school capacity and sewerage capacity permit restrictions at the County’s KNSG Wastewater Treatment Plant. In addition to these infrastructure challenges, the County must contemplate sustainable and resilient land use policies in the face of necessary hazard planning.

During this planning cycle, the community finds itself nearing the limits of adequate public facilities including, transportation infrastructure on its state and local roads, the Chesapeake Bay Bridge, local school capacity and sewerage capacity permit restrictions at the County’s KNSG Wastewater Treatment Plant. plan_areas.community_vision: In 2035, Prince George’s County is the community of choice for families, businesses, and workers in the region. It is distinguished by strong, green, and healthy communities; a competitive, innovative, and adaptive economy; vibrant and walkable mixed-use centers; quality open space; restored ecosystems; and iconic destinations. It meets the diverse needs of all Prince Georgians and embraces and builds on the momentum generated by new residents, technology, and business opportunities.

Bowie aims to continue its trajectory as a desirable and sustainable 'bedroom community' known for its strong sense of community and impeccable resident services. Situated conveniently between Washington D.C., Baltimore, and Annapolis, Bowie has experienced responsible growth, becoming an increasingly diverse and educated community. The vision for the future involves leveraging its assets, such as Bowie State University, to become a recreation tourism hub and attract more professional, scientific, and technical service sector jobs. The city is focused on enhancing its quality of life through creative placemaking, expanding its trail network, and continuing to be a leader in environmental sustainability, with goals to reduce emissions and improve energy efficiency.

plan_areas.community_vision: In 2035, Prince George’s County is the community of choice for families, businesses, and workers in the region. It is distinguished by strong, green, and healthy communities; a competitive, innovative, and adaptive economy; vibrant and walkable mixed-use centers; quality open space; restored ecosystems; and iconic destinations. It meets the diverse needs of all Prince Georgians and embraces and builds on the momentum generated by new residents, technology, and business opportunities.

It also prioritizes community well-being by improving housing quality, increasing mobility for pedestrians and cyclists, supporting seniors to age in place, and fostering an inclusive community through dedicated programs and a future community center.

plan_areas.community_vision: In 2035, Prince George’s County is the community of choice for families, businesses, and workers in the region. It meets the diverse needs of all Prince Georgians and embraces and builds on the momentum generated by new residents, technology, and business opportunities.

Montgomery County aspires to accommodate future growth by becoming more urban, diverse, and interconnected. The vision is for a future with economically competitive and complete communities that foster a stronger sense of trust and inclusiveness among people from different backgrounds. The plan guides the county to leverage growth and redevelopment to create places that improve environmental quality, support active lifestyles, encourage interaction, and address historic inequities. It seeks to make difficult decisions and take bold steps to adapt to social, environmental, demographic, and economic shifts, ensuring the county continues to be a desirable place to live and work.

As the county plans for the future, it should continue to find ways to address the specific needs of the vulnerable populations impacted by the hidden costs of poverty and determine more ways to design communities to reduce problems associated with public health, crime, housing instability, food insecurity, and segregation.

Improve awareness of and multi-modal access to the Agricultural Reserve for the public to experience and directly benefit from this valuable resource for locally grown food, outdoor recreation, and tourism.

Many Prince Georgians also do not have convenient access to a range of food options. plan_areas.community_vision: Baltimore envisions a future of harmony, inclusivity, and prosperity, where every child can thrive regardless of their zip code and residents are empowered to shape the city's growth. The community aspires to heal historical divides, championing vibrant, safe neighborhoods for all ages. This vision includes transformational growth that respects cultural heritage, efficient and transparent governance, and a commitment to environmental stewardship and carbon neutrality. The city aims to nurture an economy where small businesses flourish, ensure community safety through collective action, and promote holistic well-being by acknowledging and rectifying past injustices.

Baltimore's vision is to foster inclusive economic growth and enhance its competitiveness by supporting its diverse neighborhoods, commercial corridors, and small businesses, particularly those owned by minorities and women. The city aims to create a more equitable, resilient, and sustainable community by building on existing assets, improving transportation efficiency, promoting diverse and affordable housing, and addressing historical disinvestment. The overarching goal is to create a Standard of Care that ensures the physical, social, emotional, and economic well-being for all residents, businesses, and stakeholders, guided by an equity lens in all planning and investment decisions.

fresh_food_need_quotes: One of the most prominent is food insecurity or lack of access to healthy food. According to Feeding America, as of 2020, approximately 15.5 percent of the City’s residents are considered to suffer from food insecurity and subsequent effects.

Revitalization Goals: Use food as a catalyst to address health, economic, and environmental disparities in Healthy Food Priority Areas, areas where residents face compounded challenges in accessing healthy foods.

Food insecurity is a lack of consistent access to sufficient food that can result from a variety of physical, social and economic factors. Food deserts, unemployment, housing cost burdens, food costs, insufficient SNAP benefits and health are just a few of the interrelated causes leading to food insecurity.
Create jobs and job training opportunities and increase access to locally grown, healthy foods in Baltimore’s food deserts by creating new farms on vacant land.
In 2021, a Maryland Food Bank survey found that 33% of residents said they were food insecure. This number increased from 27% in 2017.

A mixed-use development that includes affordable housing, cultural amenities, community space, healthy food access, and green space, supported by the Red Line will generate significant revenue while bringing new investment to the underserved areas along the Route 40 corridor.
...many of Baltimore’s Black neighborhoods, the “Black Butterfly”, are also Healthy Food Priority Areas, meaning they lack access to nutritious foods.
fresh_food_planning_quotes: The City is also pursuing a reinvestment strategy for its public markets... Recognizing the need for fresh food access, and the stabilizing force that these markets can have on the neighborhood, the City has proceeded with design planning and/or Requests for Proposals for all of the city-owned markets... these market reinvestments are intended to position these markets as neighborhood commercial anchors and expand community availability to healthy foods.

In 2022, the City announced its intent to revise Charm City Circulator routes to include neighborhoods where significant percentages of residents do not own cars and lack convenient access to downtown, employment connections, medical services, and retail. Revised service routes would add Cherry Hill and West Baltimore and the Purple Line would be extended to the Waverly Giant on East 33rd Street as part of efforts to increase access to fresh food options.
Identifying sites that would be amenable to attracting a supermarket.
In addition to a racetrack, future redevelopment is likely to include grocery store, hotel, and workforce housing.

The goal of the City’s Food Policy is to build an equitable and resilient food system to mitigate the negative impacts associated with food insecurity... by: improving access to healthy affordable food, increasing produce distribution and incentivization, and addressing the food supply chain failure by building the BIPOC local food production supply chain.

The heart of the PSO Transformation Plan is creating a modern and thriving mixed-use community. This will be done by replacing 629 obsolete public housing units at Perkins Homes and redeveloping the former Somerset Homes site with over 1,350 units of mixed-income rental housing... a new full-service grocery store will be located at the former Somerset Homes site.
incentive_childcare_advice: Consider the Child Care Capital Support Revolving Loan Fund for no-interest loans for capital expenses, and the Maryland Industrial Development Financing Authority (MIDFA) which offers insurance for loans if your project is in a Priority Funding Area.

Explore the Child and Adult Care Food Program and Team Nutrition Grants which provide funding or reimbursements for meal and nutrition costs, and the The Judith P. Hoyer Early Child Care and Education Enhancement Program for accreditation and professional development grants.

If your facility requires lead paint removal, the Lead Hazard Reduction Loan and Grant Program is available, and you can participate in Maryland EXCELS to enhance quality ratings and receive support for exceeding licensing standards. Small or expanding childcare businesses should investigate the Neighborhood BusinessWorks loan program, available in Priority Funding Areas and Sustainable Communities.
incentive_fresh_food_advice: As your business is located in Baltimore City, investigate the Grocery Store Tax Credit which offers a 10-year, 80 percent personal property tax credit for grocery stores in designated incentive areas that meet investment and fresh food space requirements.

Consider the More Jobs For Marylanders Program for tax incentives related to job creation, especially if your grocery store is located in an Opportunity Zone (which are Tier 1 Areas) or other revitalization areas in Baltimore City.

Explore the Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants and Children (WIC), as store owners are an eligible sector, allowing you to provide supplemental foods to families. New or expanding grocery businesses can also seek financing through the Neighborhood BusinessWorks loan program, which supports small businesses in Priority Funding Areas and Sustainable Communities.

This vision includes transformational growth that respects cultural heritage, efficient and transparent governance, and a commitment to environmental stewardship and carbon neutrality. The city aims to nurture an economy where small businesses flourish, ensure community safety through collective action, and promote holistic well-being by acknowledging and rectifying past injustices.

Baltimore's vision is to foster inclusive economic growth and enhance its competitiveness by supporting its diverse neighborhoods, commercial corridors, and small businesses, particularly those owned by minorities and women. The city aims to create a more equitable, resilient, and sustainable community by building on existing assets, improving transportation efficiency, promoting diverse and affordable housing, and addressing historical disinvestment. The overarching goal is to create a Standard of Care that ensures the physical, social, emotional, and economic well-being for all residents, businesses, and stakeholders, guided by an equity lens in all planning and investment decisions.

fresh_food_need_quotes: One of the most prominent is food insecurity or lack of access to healthy food. According to Feeding America, as of 2020, approximately 15.5 percent of the City’s residents are considered to suffer from food insecurity and subsequent effects.

Revitalization Goals: Use food as a catalyst to address health, economic, and environmental disparities in Healthy Food Priority Areas, areas where residents face compounded challenges in accessing healthy foods.

Food insecurity is a lack of consistent access to sufficient food that can result from a variety of physical, social and economic factors. Food deserts, unemployment, housing cost burdens, food costs, insufficient SNAP benefits and health are just a few of the interrelated causes leading to food insecurity.
Create jobs and job training opportunities and increase access to locally grown, healthy foods in Baltimore’s food deserts by creating new farms on vacant land.
In 2021, a Maryland Food Bank survey found that 33% of residents said they were food insecure. This number increased from 27% in 2017.

A mixed-use development that includes affordable housing, cultural amenities, community space, healthy food access, and green space, supported by the Red Line will generate significant revenue while bringing new investment to the underserved areas along the Route 40 corridor.
...many of Baltimore’s Black neighborhoods, the “Black Butterfly”, are also Healthy Food Priority Areas, meaning they lack access to nutritious foods.
fresh_food_planning_quotes: The City is also pursuing a reinvestment strategy for its public markets... Recognizing the need for fresh food access, and the stabilizing force that these markets can have on the neighborhood, the City has proceeded with design planning and/or Requests for Proposals for all of the city-owned markets... these market reinvestments are intended to position these markets as neighborhood commercial anchors and expand community availability to healthy foods.

In 2022, the City announced its intent to revise Charm City Circulator routes to include neighborhoods where significant percentages of residents do not own cars and lack convenient access to downtown, employment connections, medical services, and retail. Revised service routes would add Cherry Hill and West Baltimore and the Purple Line would be extended to the Waverly Giant on East 33rd Street as part of efforts to increase access to fresh food options.
Identifying sites that would be amenable to attracting a supermarket.
In addition to a racetrack, future redevelopment is likely to include grocery store, hotel, and workforce housing.

The goal of the City’s Food Policy is to build an equitable and resilient food system to mitigate the negative impacts associated with food insecurity... by: improving access to healthy affordable food, increasing produce distribution and incentivization, and addressing the food supply chain failure by building the BIPOC local food production supply chain.

The heart of the PSO Transformation Plan is creating a modern and thriving mixed-use community. This will be done by replacing 629 obsolete public housing units at Perkins Homes and redeveloping the former Somerset Homes site with over 1,350 units of mixed-income rental housing... a new full-service grocery store will be located at the former Somerset Homes site.
incentive_childcare_advice: Consider the Child Care Capital Support Revolving Loan Fund for no-interest loans to cover capital expenses for your facility, especially if you participate in the State Department of Education’s Child Care Scholarship Program.
Apply for the Child and Adult Care Food Program to offset meal and supplement costs for licensed non-residential childcare services.
Explore the Maryland Industrial Development Financing Authority (MIDFA) program, which offers insurance and bond financing specifically for day care providers located in Priority Funding Areas.
incentive_fresh_food_advice: If opening or renovating a grocery store, apply for the Baltimore City Grocery Store Tax Credit to receive an 80% personal property tax credit for 10 years on investments in new equipment and facilities within designated incentive areas.
As the area is within an Opportunity Zone, your grocery business may be eligible for the More Jobs For Marylanders Program, offering state income tax credits for creating new full-time jobs.

Investigate the Neighborhood BusinessWorks loan program which provides financing to new or expanding small businesses and nonprofit organizations located in Priority Funding Areas and Sustainable Communities.

This vision includes transformational growth that respects cultural heritage, efficient and transparent governance, and a commitment to environmental stewardship and carbon neutrality. The city aims to nurture an economy where small businesses flourish, ensure community safety through collective action, and promote holistic well-being by acknowledging and rectifying past injustices.

Baltimore's vision is to foster inclusive economic growth and enhance its competitiveness by supporting its diverse neighborhoods, commercial corridors, and small businesses, particularly those owned by minorities and women. The city aims to create a more equitable, resilient, and sustainable community by building on existing assets, improving transportation efficiency, promoting diverse and affordable housing, and addressing historical disinvestment. The overarching goal is to create a Standard of Care that ensures the physical, social, emotional, and economic well-being for all residents, businesses, and stakeholders, guided by an equity lens in all planning and investment decisions.

This initiative is fundamentally about equity and justice, resilience, and health—a transformation of place supported by new connections, jobs, wealth-generation, and quality of life amenities that extend beyond the built environment.
